Description
The UTEP Landscape Ecology Lab is considering applications for a Fall 2027 PhD student to begin at the University of Texas at El Paso through the EEB Program. The student will work on the remote sensing of forest vegetation structure (roots), soil ecology, and ecosystem function with a collaborative team (SERC, UCONN, IU, Kenyon College) at the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (SERC) (on objectives for NSF Award #2621909).

Minimum requirements: At least a 3.2 GPA, previous independent research experience including in the field, must obtain a US driver’s license. This project has a heavy field component requiring work at SERC (Edgewater, Maryland) for 1-2 semesters for long-hours outdoors and in possible challenging weather. The student will be based in El Paso, TX for the remainder of the UTEP PhD program when not doing field research at SERC. 

Benefits for UTEP PhD students: Graduate assistantship, student health insurance, tuition remission. 

Interested applicants can contact Dr. La Rue (ealarue@utep.edu) with your CV (including any publications), a 1-page summary of your research/career goals, and contact info for 2 references.
Contact
Elizabeth La Rue
ealarue@utep.edu (preferred contact method)

Description
A funded PhD/MS position is available in the Lichtenberg Lab starting summer or fall 2027. This position is part of a USDA-funded project investigating how ranch management impacts pollinator, plant, and soil microbe biodiversity both directly and through habitat modification. The selected student will focus on the pollinator component. Research activities will include fieldwork at local North Texas ranches, insect identification, and analyzing a multi-year dataset from the ranches. Funding includes semester and summer salary, a tuition scholarship, and health insurance for PhD students or a Health Assistance Scholarship for MS students. The Lichtenberg Lab combines community and behavioral ecology to study plant-animal interactions, pollinator foraging and insect biodiversity. We are particularly interested in how land use change and land management practices affect these phenomena. The lab is committed to providing an inclusive and supportive environment to trainees from diverse backgrounds. More details at https://cos.unt.edu/biology/lichtenberg-lab/index.html.
 Application: Please contact Dr. Elinor Lichtenberg (elichten@unt.edu) before applying. Send your CV, information on relevant experiences, the degree and kinds of questions you are interested in, and unofficial transcripts.
 The University of North Texas is a R1 university located in Denton, near Dallas and Fort Worth. We are a Minority Serving Institution, a Hispanic Serving Institution and a Bee Campus. Department of Biological Sciences researchers study diverse topics, including conservation, sustainable production of plant-based materials, environmental education, remote sensing and neuroscience. The Lichtenberg Lab participates in the Advanced Environmental Research Institute, an interdisciplinary group that seeks to find solutions to pressing environmental issues. Denton is a vibrant college town known for its live music, and was ranked No. 1 Best Small Town in America. North Texas offers many opportunities for outdoor activities such as hiking, swimming, bird watching, wildflower viewing and horseback riding. Dallas and Fort Worth provide additional attractions, including museums, theater, restaurants and pro sports.
Contact
Elinor Lichtenberg
elichten@unt.edu (preferred contact method)

title: Ph.D. Teaching Assistantship for Bat Ecology (tuition scholarship for 3 years)
description:
Ph.D. Teaching Assistantship for Bat Ecology (tuition scholarship for 3 years)
Texas State University (State) | https://www.bio.txst.edu/
Details
Application Deadline:
08/05/2026
Published:
07/21/2026
Starting Date:
after 1/15/2027
Hours per Week:
40
Salary:
$31,615 per year
Education Required:
Masters
Experience Required:
at least 2 years
Location:
Texas State University (San Marcos, Texas)
Tags:
Graduate Opportunities
Description
 Overview
I am seeking an outstanding individual to pursue a doctoral degree in bat ecology at Texas State University. I am particularly interested in applicants that can use already collected acoustic data from Texas and South Africa, combined with the North American Bat Monitoring Program database to answer various population and community ecology questions of their interest.  There will be opportunity for field-work if the applicant desires including monitoring bats through mist netting, thermal and IR cameras, and acoustics. The successful applicant will work with me and their committee to formulate their own research questions and be expected to complete the writing and quantitative components of their dissertation.
 
The position requires teaching two lab sections during the long semesters with pay at $31,615/year ($3,512.85/month for 9 months) . There will be opportunities for further funding through competitive scholarships and grants. Tuition will be waived for three years, any longer with have Texas resident tuition rate. 

Research Focus
I have bat acoustic data collected from Texas and South Africa and expect the student to formulate independent research questions and hypotheses with advice from myself and their committee. I also have supplies such as mist nets, thermal and IR cameras, acoustic recorders, etc. to formulate a field-based study. Texas is home to the most number of bat species and the largest bat colonies in the world. Central Texas alone has over 100 million Brazilian free-tailed bats so there are many research possibilities.

Qualification
A MS degree in wildlife biology/management or closely-related field is required. Excellent communication and time-management skills, a strong work ethic, and attention to detail also are essential. The candidate must also have a valid Texas driver’s license, or be able to obtain a valid Texas driver’s license immediately upon starting.  This is a fully-immersive Ph.D. program and the student must reside in San Marcos. 

The teaching assistantships are competitive at Texas State University. To qualify, it will be necessary to have a 3.0 or higher GPA and experience presenting research at conferences and preferred to have at least one peer-reviewed publication. 

Deadline 
Applicants will first apply with Dr. Sarah Fritts and then will be added to the pool of Ph.D. applicants for the Department of Biology to compete for the teaching assistantship. 

By August 5th, please send only one PDF file with a cover letter outlining your qualifications, research interests and experiences including potential research questions you may be interested in pursuing in this Ph.D. role, copy of all transcripts that also includes coursework and overall GPA, GRE scores (if available), a CV, contact details of three references, and an example of your writing to Dr. Fritts (fritts.sarah@txstate.edu). 

Texas State University 
Texas State University has been an emerging research university with plans to become R1 in 2027. This position is in the Department of Biology, which is a large and multidisciplinary department with many strong, well-funded research programs and a wide array of course offerings for undergraduate and graduate students. Our faculty engage in innovative research meant to uncover new knowledge and provide that knowledge to the state, country, and the world.  Through our education, scholarship, and outreach activities, the department enhances the image of the university by using the life sciences to help meet current and future needs of society. 

 

Contact
Dr. Sarah Fritts
fritts.sarah@txstate.edu (preferred contact method)

description:
Graduate student (M.S.) – Roadside Pollinator Habitat Restoration and Native Bee Ecology (Auburn University)
Auburn University (State) | https://www.auburn.edu/
Details

09/15/2026
Published:
07/23/2026

after 1/11/2027

40

$25,000 per year
Education Required:
Bachelors
Experience Required:
none
Location:
Auburn, Alabama
Tags:
Graduate Opportunities
Description
Application deadline: Review of applications will begin now through September 15, 2026, or until a suitable candidate is found.

Start date: January 2027

Project description and responsibilities: The Auburn University Native Bee Lab, housed within the Auburn University Bee Center, is seeking a highly motivated M.S. student to join our research program focused on pollinator conservation and habitat restoration in the southeastern United States.
The successful applicant will work on a collaborative research project funded by the Alabama Department of Transportation (ALDOT) to evaluate strategies for establishing and managing native wildflower habitats along roadsides to benefit native pollinators. Research will focus on assessing how vegetation management practices, including selective herbicide applications and other restoration techniques, influence wildflower establishment, plant community composition, and native bee communities. The project will provide science-based recommendations for improving roadside habitat while maintaining transportation safety and infrastructure needs.

Responsibilities will include:
• Establishing and maintaining field experiments throughout Alabama.
• Conducting vegetation surveys and native bee sampling.
• Identifying plants and insect pollinators (training provided as needed).
• Assisting with data management, statistical analyses, and GIS-based habitat assessments.
• Presenting research findings to scientific audiences and project stakeholders, including ALDOT personnel.
• Publishing results in peer-reviewed scientific journals.

The selected student will be expected to assume a leadership role within the laboratory by mentoring undergraduate researchers and assisting with laboratory and field operations. Numerous opportunities exist to develop expertise in native bee taxonomy, pollination ecology, restoration ecology, experimental design, and scientific communication.

The student will also participate in the collaborative atmosphere of the Auburn University Native Bee Lab through outreach activities, guest lectures, extension programming, and interdisciplinary research projects.

Opportunities for collaboration are extensive within Auburn University's Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology, the College of Agriculture, and with state and federal agencies, including the Alabama Department of Transportation.

Duration: Approximately three years

Salary range and other benefits: Starting salary of $25,000 for M.S. program with opportunities for advancement depending on performance. The individual will be assigned a Graduate Research Assistant position that includes a full tuition waiver.

Required qualifications: An undergraduate degree in Biology, Ecology, Entomology, Botany, or a related field from an accredited institution in the United States or an equivalent institution abroad is required to begin a M.S. program. The selected individual must meet eligibility requirements to work in the United States at the time of appointment.

Desired qualifications: Experience contributing to native pollinator research is ideal. Specifically, experience with plant and native bee identification is optimal. However, finding an individual who is hard-working, collaborative, organized, a team player, and has a strong passion for learning is equally important.
Application description: Complete applications must include: 1) a one-page cover letter that addresses your experiences and goals with respect to this position as well as how you meet the required and desired qualifications; 2) curriculum vitae; 3) contact information for three references; and 4) copies of all post-secondary transcripts.

Application submission: All materials should be compiled as a single PDF document and submitted to Dr. Anthony Abbate (aunativebeelab@gmail.com). Please include ‘Graduate Student Opportunity’ in the email subject line.

The University: A Carnegie R1 university, Auburn is a public flagship land-grant institution with a student enrollment of more than 30,000. The University provides instruction in approximately 70 academic departments, performs graduate research and public service across a variety of program areas, and is home to a vibrant community that enjoys a college-town feel. The University is located in the city of Auburn in east-central Alabama, near the metropolitan areas of Birmingham, AL, and Atlanta, GA, as well as scenic escapes like the southern Appalachians and the Gulf of Mexico.

The Department: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology is administered by the University’s historic College of Agriculture. It houses over 20 faculty, 5 support staff, and more than 50 graduate students, all of whom work towards executing the University’s research, instruction, and extension missions. Additional information can be found at http://enpp.auburn.edu.

The Laboratory: The Auburn University Native Bee Lab is housed within the Auburn University Bee Center, a multidisciplinary program dedicated to advancing bee research, education, and extension. The Native Bee Lab currently consists of two graduate students supported by one faculty member, one laboratory manager, three technicians, and multiple undergraduate students and local stakeholders. Alongside our collaborators from across the globe, the Native Bee Lab team works to promote bee health through research, instruction, extension, and outreach activities.
Contact
Anthony Abbate
aunativebeelab@gmail.com (preferred contact method)

description:
Graduate Services Assistant in Insect Vector Ecology
Arizona State University (State)
Details
Application Deadline:
07/31/2026
Published:
07/20/2026
Starting Date:
after 8/17/2026
Hours per Week:
at least 20
Salary:
up to $31,200 per year
Education Required:
Bachelors
Experience Required:
none
Location:
Mesa, Arizona
Description
A Graduate Services Assistant position is available for an MS student to support research on climate-dependent dynamics of disease-causing insects in the Lyberger Lab at Arizona State University. This position is well suited for a student interested in quantitative ecology, ecological modeling, population dynamics, disease ecology, and the effects of environmental variation on insect vectors. Broadly, this work will contribute to projects examining how temperature and climate variability influence insect population dynamics and potential disease transmission risk. Primary responsibilities may include conducting literature reviews, processing environmental or climate data, developing statistical or mechanistic models, and preparing presentations and manuscripts. Depending on project needs and the student’s training goals, work may also involve experimental design, insect collection or rearing, and integration of experimental data with environmental or population-level datasets.

Required qualifications: a Bachelor’s degree in biology, ecology, environmental science, entomology, applied mathematics, statistics, data science, or a related field; strong academic record; strong interest in quantitative ecology, ecological modeling, population dynamics, disease ecology, climate change biology, or insect vectors.
Preferred qualifications: familiarity with R, Python, or similar programming languages; experience working with spatial data, remote sensing products, or large environmental datasets; experience with scientific writing and data management; ability to work independently and manage large datasets.
 The student must be able to begin in person in Mesa, AZ. The anticipated start date is August 17, 2026, although a January 2027 start date may be possible.
 Funding and Enrollment
This is a Graduate Services Assistant appointment:
20 hours/week during the academic year and summer
$1,200 biweekly stipend, up to $31,200 annually
This appointment does not include tuition remission or health insurance benefits. Tuition estimator: https://tuition.asu.edu/cost/tuition-estimator
The student will enroll in the M.S. program in Applied Biological Sciences in the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts.
 Application Instructions
Applicants must first be selected for the GSA position before submitting their ASU graduate application.
To apply for the GSA position, email a single PDF with the following materials in this order: (1) a cover letter describing research interests and career goals, (2) a CV or resume, (3) contact information for three references, and (4) unofficial transcripts. Name the file as Lastname_Firstname.pdf.
Send materials to Dr. Kelsey Lyberger at Kelsey.lyberger@asu.edu.
Application deadline: July 31, 2026.
Contact
Kelsey Lyberger
kelsey.lyberger@asu.edu (preferred contact method)

Position Information
Position Overview
Essential Job Duties | Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. Working for NC State Extension allows you to teach without being tied to a classroom and school bell. Check out this video on what it’s like to work for NC State Extension.

No two days in Extension are ever the same, there is always something new! Extension Agents are active in their communities and often need to meet the clients when and where they are available. This is not your typical desk job!

While our employees are located in NC County offices, they reap the benefits of employment at NC State University. Some of our benefits include:· Paid time off· Paid tuition· Health Insurance· Flexible Scheduling
· Retirement Savings· Supplemental Benefits Programs· WolfPerks!
You Belong Here! At NC State, our goal is for all employees to reach their fullest potential at work. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition(https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone.

Primary Purpose of Position
This position will be responsible for Horticulture programming in Dare County. The Horticulture Agent is responsible for planning, implementing and evaluating an outcome-based program addressing issues and opportunities identified in Dare County. The agent in this position must have technical competence in both consumer and commercial horticulture and in the delivery of non-formal education programs, and the identification of plants and pests and the diagnosis of plant problems. The agent in this position develops and works with stakeholder-based committees that provide direction for Extension programs; works with community organizations to effectively link Extension with local resources and clients; and assists effectively with recruiting, training, and managing Extension Master Gardener and other volunteers to expand outreach efforts. In addition, this agent will provide support to community gardens and work towards developing a youth horticulture program.

Primary Function of Organizational Unit
North Carolina Cooperative Extension gives our residents easy access to the resources and expertise of NC State University and NC A&T State University. Through educational programs, publications, and events, Cooperative Extension field faculty deliver unbiased, research-based information to North Carolina citizens.

Dare County has a strong and thriving Extension Master Gardener volunteer program. The 75 Master Gardener volunteers regularly assist at the Dare County Extension Center, maintain the Outer Banks Arboretum, and have responded to more than 10,539 contacts in 2024 and provided hours of service equaling over $203,000. The group provides educational programs for its members as well as delivers programs throughout the community.
Dare County is located in northeastern North Carolina along the Atlantic seaboard. Dare County stretches along almost 110 miles of shoreline known as the Outer Banks. The County seat at Manteo is approximately 200 miles east of Raleigh, the State capital, and 90 miles south of Virginia Beach-Norfolk, Virginia, metropolitan area. The County contains much of what is known as North Carolina’s “Outer Banks” resort and vacation areas and contains approximately two-thirds of the North Carolina coastline. Six municipalities are located within the county: Duck, Kill Devil Hills, Kitty Hawk, Manteo, Nags Head and Southern Shores. Dare County has a permanent population of approximately 38,000 residents.

For information about Dare County visit https://www.darenc.gov/
To learn more about the NCCE Dare County Center go to https://dare.ces.ncsu.edu/
Duties and Responsibilities
The Agent works with homeowners, community groups, commercial horticultural crop producers, professional landscape and turf professionals, and others to increase their knowledge of horticultural issues and implementation of best management practices.
Additional responsibilities include assisting with recruiting and training new Master Gardeners, pesticide education as it pertains to horticulture and the green industry, and developing and coordinating youth horticulture programs.
This person must be self-directed, having the ability to juggle multiple responsibilities and schedules, have effective oral and written communication skills, and be willing to work with broad audiences. Grant writing and project management experience is essential. Computer, organization, interpersonal and networking skills are crucial for success. Ability to effectively deliver information via mass media including television, radio and social media is expected. Candidates must be willing to work with the staff to support the entire Extension program.
The person in this position must possess a high degree of horticulture subject matter competence and excellent people and communication skills, be computer literate, and have the necessary education and experience to lead a strong Extension education program in the assigned areas.
Primary Function of Organizational Unit
Other Work/Responsibilities | The professional in this position must be energetic, enjoy working with individuals as well as groups, be able to work with audiences, and have the ability to manage multiple tasks with little supervision. He/she must possess a high degree of subject matter competence, have the ability to work independently and as a team member interdisciplinary across subject matters as well as develop subject-matter-related 4-H youth horticulture programming.

Description
 *Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis.

ARS Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), located in Ames, Iowa.

The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence. The mission of the USDA-ARS Corn Insects and Crop Genetics Research Unit (CICGRU) in Ames, Iowa, is to increase crop productivity and sustainability. The unit achieves this through basic and applied research focused on managing insect pests, improving crop genetics, and studying host-pathogen interactions in cereals and legumes.

Research Project: The USDA research project that you will gain training on has a mission to provide stewardship of soybean and other major legume genetic, genomic, and phenotypic datasets, to support research and crop improvement. Basic and applied research is also conducted within this project. You will use methods in computational biology to identify conserved genetic elements across a range of taxonomic depths, to help determine elements that have been important in the many crops in the legume plant family. This fellowship will play a part in analyzing new genomic data, to help utilize variation available in USDA gene banks and to identify and use high-value genetic elements for improvement of these crops. This opportunity will mostly be conducted in a Unix environment and on high-performance computing equipment. 

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will have the opportunity to learn to: (a) apply methods in computational biology, genetics, and artificial intelligence, including: statistical methods of marker-trait association, methods for determining syntenic relationships and for calculating and representing pan-genome relationships, methods for inferring gene families and for inferring evolutionary events from large collections of gene families; (b) conduct writing within scientific manuscripts.

Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Steven Cannon (steven.cannon@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: October 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.

Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of ARS and is contingent on the availability of funds.

Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.

Participant Stipend: The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. The anticipated stipend range is $75,284 - $90,234 annually.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.

ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and ARS. Participants do not become employees of USDA, ARS, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.

Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process, please email ORISE.ARS.Midwest@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.

Qualifications
The qualified candidate should have received a doctoral degree in the one of the relevant fields. Degree must have been received within the past five years.

Preferred skills

Knowledge of basic methods in genomic sequence analysis and plant genetics. 
Unix scripting, knowledge of a scripting language such as Python, Perl, awk, or R, knowledge of computational methods for aligning genic sequence and calculating phylogenetic trees, and knowledge of statistical methods for use in interpreting sequence homology results.
Botanical knowledge (e.g. knowledge of major taxonomic groupings in the angiosperms).

Description

ARS Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS), National Center for Agricultural Utilization Research, located at Peoria, Illinois.

The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.

Research Project: You will receive mentorship and training in plant-pathogen interactions between wheat and mycotoxigenic fungi, with a focus on understanding factors that contribute to improved wheat resilience to fungal disease. Under the guidance of your mentor, you will study Fusarium Head Blight (FHB), one of the most significant diseases affecting wheat production, grain quality, and food safety worldwide.

You will learn how transcriptomic and metabolomic approaches are used to investigate plant defense responses and support wheat breeding strategies aimed at improving disease resistance and maintaining grain nutritional quality. Training activities will include analyzing existing datasets and generating new molecular and metabolic data using advanced sequencing technologies and bioinformatics methods.

Throughout the project, you will develop hands-on experience in plant physiology, nutritional assessment, disease severity evaluation, transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis, and scientific data interpretation. You will also gain experience applying computational and laboratory techniques to agricultural research questions related to crop resilience, plant health, and food security.

Learn more about the research being conducted at NCAUR: https://www.ars.usda.gov/midwest-area/peoria-il/national-center-for-agricultural-utilization-research/mycotoxin-prevention-and-applied-microbiology-research/

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of your mentor, you will have the opportunity to:

Develop bioinformatics skills
Learn plant pathology, plant physiology methodology and skillset
Learn to collaborate in a multi-disciplinary research group
Develop presentation and speaking skills
Refine problem solving skills
Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is William Hay (william.hay@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).

Anticipated Appointment Start Date: 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.

Appointment Length: The appointment will be for two years.

Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.

Participant Stipend: The participant will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. The anticipated stipend is $74,678 minimum, annually.

Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.

ARS Office/Lab and Location: A research opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS).

The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.

Research Project: The mission of the U.S. Vegetable Laboratory is: a) to improve genetic populations of vegetable crops by combining resistance to diseases and pests (nematodes, insects, and weeds) with favored quality characters and improved yield potentials; and b) to develop knowledge on disease and pest biology, ecology, and epidemiology that can be used as a basis for the development and implementation of new, reliable, environmentally sound integrated management systems that rely on host resistance, biocontrol, and natural compounds rather than conventional pesticides. You will be a part of a project to learn about conducting experiments and data collection on food production and genetic improvement of various crops, especially vegetables and fruits, under abiotic and biotic stress in controlled environment.

Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will trained to:

Design and implement integrated pest management on emerging and important diseases on vegetable crops under controlled environments;
Co-develop effective disinfectants and other treatments against plant diseases and pests for sustainable crop production in controlled environment; 
Identify and help develop new germplasm or cultivars with resistance to emerging or important diseases or pathogen-vectors using molecular-based tools or biotechnology; 
Co-develop plant genetic materials with resistance to emerging tobamoviruses, tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) in tomato and cucumber green mottle mosaic virus (CGMMV) in cucurbits. 
Screen plant germplasm and co-develop plant genetic materials with tolerance to abiotic stresses (salt, heat, or drought tolerance). 
Improve controlled environment agriculture for crop production, including plant growth, fruit production, crop harvesting, food processing, and nutritional analysis.  
Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Kai-Shu Ling (kai.ling@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).

Description
 Kenyon College invites applications for a tenure-track position in the Departments of Environmental Studies and Biology (Freshwater Ecosystem or Landscape Ecology) starting in July 2027. We seek a broadly trained ecologist with expertise in freshwater ecosystem or landscape ecology, with an interest in contributing to an interdisciplinary department. To complement current faculty expertise, we seek candidates whose research focuses on regional or global ecological or biogeochemical processes, preferably in freshwater systems. Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to excellent teaching, including strong academic support, inclusive course experiences, and effective mentoring for our diverse student population. Teaching expectations are 5 courses per year, with 3 courses in the Environmental Studies Department (e.g., Introduction to Environmental Studies, Senior Seminar in Environmental Studies, and new lecture and/or lab courses at the upper level) and 2 courses in the Biology Department (e.g., Introductory Biology lecture or lab, Aquatic Systems Biology). Additional opportunities exist for interdisciplinary teaching and scholarship within and outside the sciences, including in Kenyon's interdisciplinary Program in Computing and the college's Science and Nature Writing initiative. We expect a vigorous research program that involves undergraduate students, leads to publications, and has potential to attract extramural funding. Applicants should hold a Ph.D degree; post-doctoral experience is preferred. We encourage applications from all groups historically underrepresented in the sciences.

A complete application will be composed of 1) a cover letter (maximum 2 pages); 2) a Curriculum Vitae (no page limit); 3) a statement of the applicant's teaching philosophy that addresses the applicant’s experiences and plans for teaching a diverse student body (maximum 2 pages); 4) a statement of the applicant’s research and scholarship that includes plans for collaborative research with undergraduates (maximum 3 pages); 5) an unofficial graduate transcript; and 6) contact information for three professional references.

All application materials must be submitted electronically through Kenyon's employment website: http://careers.kenyon.edu. Review of applications will begin on August 31, 2026. Please direct questions to Natalie Wright, Search Committee Chair (wright1@kenyon.edu).

Kenyon College is a nationally prominent, private liberal arts college where academic excellence goes hand in hand with a strong sense of community and close relationships among students and professors. Situated along the beautiful Kokosing River, with a 700-acre nature preserve, Kenyon is an ideal place to study and teach ecology. Kenyon has an established record of preparing students for graduate study and research careers, ranking 8th nationally in the proportion of STEM graduates who go on to earn doctoral degrees. Our students regularly earn nationally competitive awards, including Fulbright Fellowships and National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program awards.

Description
The Johnson Laboratory (www.johnsonlaboratory.com) at the University of Colorado is seeking a highly motivated Ph.D. student to join our research program in marine disease ecology and conservation beginning in Fall 2027. This project offers a unique opportunity to investigate an emerging parasite outbreak in coral reef ecosystems, combining fieldwork in the Caribbean, laboratory experiments, archival museum research, behavioral ecology, and quantitative modeling. The position is supported through federal funding and includes opportunities for conference travel and interdisciplinary collaborations. The selected student will join a collaborative and highly supportive research group dedicated to understanding how parasites shape ecological communities and ecosystem function.

 
Quantifying the emergence and ecological consequences of a marine parasite outbreak

 Parasites are increasingly recognized as important drivers of ecological change, yet their effects on marine ecosystems remain poorly understood. This project focuses on Black Spot Syndrome (BSS), a parasitic disease that causes visible lesions on reef fishes and is increasing in parts of the Caribbean. Because BSS disproportionately affects herbivorous fishes that play critical roles in maintaining coral reef health, understanding its emergence may have important implications for reef conservation and management.

 The selected student will help address questions such as:

 How have the prevalence, infection intensity, and geographic distribution of Scaphanocephalus changed across the Caribbean over the past 150 years? 
What environmental and ecological factors drive variation in disease risk across local and regional scales? 
How do parasite infections alter fish behavior and influence ecosystem processes? 
 Research approaches may include Caribbean field studies, behavioral experiments, analysis of historical museum collections, spatial and ecological modeling, and participation in outreach and education programs in both Colorado and the Caribbean.

 
Desired qualifications

We welcome applicants with interests in disease ecology, marine biology, conservation biology, parasitology, ecology, fisheries, or related disciplines. Experience in any of the following is particularly valuable: marine fieldwork, snorkeling or SCUBA diving, boat operations, fisheries sampling, quantitative ecology and statistics, geographic information systems (GIS), and experimental design and data analysis. 

 
Application materials

Please submit a single PDF containing:

Curriculum vitae 
Statement of research interests and previous research experience including relevant marine field experience (e.g., fishing, boating, snorkeling, SCUBA diving)
Explanation of why you are interested in this project and the Johnson Laboratory 
Description of your long-term career goals 
  
Please email application materials to Pieter.Johnson@colorado.edu with the subject line:
"Marine Prospective Graduate Student"
Applications received by October 4, 2026 will receive full consideration.
